root_idea.summary: An opening made by piercing or hollowing, especially the opening of a shirt or similar garment.
root_idea.development: The root is connected with making an opening or cavity, possibly through an underlying wāw alternation. From this developed the garment opening and related derived usages.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular noun citation form جَيْبٌ.

senses.definition: An opening in a garment, especially the opening at the neck or upper breast—the bosom opening.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences use inflected singular and plural forms for a garment opening. The plural occurs in 24:31, while the singular occurs in the construction “your jayb” in 27:12 and 28:32.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pocket or receptacle in a shirt or similar garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended application arising from the practice of carrying things within the bosom or opening of a garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart or inner bosom, figuratively; hence the seat of sincerity, trustworthiness, or foul character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in metaphorical expressions describing the moral or inward state of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The entrance or access-way of a land or country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative application, with a plural جُيُوبٌ also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hollowed or excavated, specifically of a sapphire in a reported traditional expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive-participial usage; variant readings of the expression are reported.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the garment opening and its extended pocket application.
Covers the figurative heart or inner-bosom sense.
Covers the entrance of a land or country.
Defines the specialized derived-form usage meaning hollowed.

cautions: The contextual gloss “bosom” is treated here as a rendering of the Quranic garment opening; the figurative heart or inner-bosom sense is separately attested as a broader Classical Arabic usage.
